warpScale.description: World units per cycle of the warp. Measured: keep it near TWICE the tile size, not far above it. A warp much coarser than the tile slides whole tiles around and leaves the motif inside each one perfectly intact, so a strongly patterned texture still reads as a pattern; a warp at roughly tile scale distorts the motif itself, which is what stops a big rock face looking stamped.

aperture.description: Disc feathers to an oval; opening fills the full local-UV quad with a narrow edge fade for a framed doorway. Place sealed architecture several metres behind it; this shader does not implement travel or collision.

lighting.description: False keeps animated water color, waves, foam and fog but removes scene-light shading and specular highlights. Useful for graphic sewer water. True preserves the standard lit ocean appearance.

textureTint.description: When set, recolor the scrolling texture by its luminance before blending, preserving visible moving detail without importing its original hue. Omit to retain the original texture colors. Combine with textureStrength to control moving detail.

texture.description: Surface texture ADDED over the procedural water, scrolled in two directions at two scales so it never reads as one tile sliding past. It contributes light rather than replacing colour, so the depth banding, shoreline foam and fresnel rim underneath all survive — the texture supplies the moving detail those cannot.

textureScale.description: World units per texture tile. Sampled in WORLD XZ, not UV, so tiling is continuous across a huge plane and independent of how the mesh happens to be unwrapped.

textureStrength.description: How far the surface reads as the TEXTURE rather than the procedural bands. 1 is texture-led (still shaded by depth, foam and fresnel); low values leave it as a faint tint over the original look.

foamPixel.description: World units per foam BLOCK. The shoreline band's breakup is sampled on a snapped grid, so the edge steps in squares of this size instead of wandering smoothly — which is what makes it sit beside nearest-filtered pixel-art terrain instead of looking airbrushed onto it. 0 disables the snap.

foamSteps.description: Quantisation levels in the foam band. Fewer = chunkier, more poster-like; 1 is a hard on/off edge.

flow.description: Texture drift in tiles per second [x, z]. The second sample layer moves at a different scale and roughly perpendicular, which is what stops the eye locking onto a single repeating direction.

flowMode.description: drift: standing water — waves and texture are laid out in WORLD space (so sheets streamed cell by cell agree along their shared edges) and drift by `flow`. channel: moving water — the geometry carries a per-vertex `flow` vector and metre uvs (a `path` ribbon with `flowSpeed` and `uvMetres`), and waves, texture and foam all travel along it at that speed: a river runs downstream and over its falls. Only use channel on geometry that has the attribute.

displace.description: Move the vertices with the waves. Right for a finely subdivided plane (the ocean); WRONG for a lake sheet (one polygon fan) or a river ribbon (two vertices across), where lifting the few vertices tilts whole triangles into faceted streaks. false keeps the wave NORMALS (lighting still moves) and leaves the geometry flat. `worldgen rivers` writes the lake and river materials with false.

wakeHeight.description: Metres of relief a wake pushes into this surface. A wake is a simulated height field (a swimmer, a boat, rain) that this material DISPLACES its vertices by and bends its normals along, so a wake DEFORMS the water instead of colouring it. On a `displace: false` sheet the geometry cannot move and only the normals respond, which still reads as ripples. 0 turns wakes off here.

wakeFoam.description: How much a wake's CRESTS also froth, in `foamColor`. Small on purpose: whitening the whole disturbed patch is what made every earlier wake read as a decal stuck to the surface. 0 = pure water motion.

cellSize.description: World units per streamed chunk cell (XZ). Must match the scene's voxelWorld cellSize.

resolution.description: Voxels per cell edge. voxelSize = cellSize / resolution — 2m voxels read as chunky low-poly, 0.5m as smooth.

bounds.description: Turns the endless noise field into CONTINENTS ringed by open ocean. Omit it and the world has no edge at all: the terrain tiles outward forever and 'world size' is only however far the CLI happened to place features. Applied inside the single shared height function, so the mesh, the cooked collider and the placement solver agree about where the coast is — the one rule this generator breaks at its peril.

minY.description: Hard floor: below this the world is solid rock, so nothing can fall out of it.

maxY.description: Hard ceiling: above this is always air (bounds the vertical march). It costs nothing where the ground is low — the meshed band is derived per cell from that cell's own terrain — so it only has to clear the highest peak the noise can produce.

base.description: Baseline ground height before any noise band. Relative to seaLevel this is what sets the land/ocean ratio.

warp.description: Domain warp of the whole heightfield — turns noise-looking hills into eroded-looking landforms.

mountainMask.description: Where mountains are ALLOWED. Without a mask, ridged noise puts peaks everywhere and the world reads as noise.

coast.description: Sea cliffs. The shoreline profile is steepened in place where a low-frequency noise says the coast is rugged, so headlands plunge into deep water and bays stay shallow and sandy. The beach BIOME needs no change: its height window is simply crossed in two metres of ground instead of forty, so sand survives only where the coast is gentle — and the `crag` rule paints the cliff face rock on its own.

dunes.description: Sand dunes: a ridged, stretched band added to the heightfield ONLY where the climate is hot and dry — the same window the desert biome uses, so the landform and the sand arrive together. This is what makes a desert a different PLACE rather than the same hills in a different colour, and the pattern generalises: any biome that should have its own landform gets a masked band like this one.

mesas.description: BADLANDS landform: a terraced plateau band, added where a zone anchor's `mesas` says so. Tables, buttes and stepped strata — the shape that reads as badland, which no amount of red texture on rolling hills achieves. The band is masked by the ZONE, so it is off everywhere unless an anchor asks for it.

ceiling.description: MAX HEIGHT: a smooth, monotonic compression of everything above `height - softness` toward `height`. It is what lets the mountain band have a big amplitude (for tall, steep flanks) without any peak punching through `maxY` and being sliced flat — and it gives every summit in the world a common sense of scale. Omit for no ceiling.

cliffs.description:
CLIFF TERRACING — the difference between marching-cubes noise and rock. fBm has a bounded gradient, so unshaped terrain arrives as rounded bubbles with no sheer face anywhere, no matter how the amplitudes are tuned. This remaps altitude within each `step` band so most of the band is spent in a short riser and the rest is a flat tread: ledges and walls, which is what a cliff is.

It shapes the MOUNTAIN band's own relief, not the finished height, and that choice is load-bearing twice over. It self-gates — the mountain mask is already zero over meadows, so terracing cannot turn a field into a wedding cake, and no slope test is needed (there is no slope to test inside `height()`: `slope()` is defined in terms of it). And it leaves the treads riding the continent and hill bands rather than dead level, which is what keeps them reading as rock ledges instead of as a contour map.

The remap is monotonic, exactly like `coast.cliff`, so the terrain stays a function — no self-intersections — and rivers/roads/towns still carve on top of the result. OFF by default; it costs one extra noise evaluation per column.

overhang.description: THE reason to use marching cubes over a heightmap: a true 3D perturbation, so cliffs undercut and arches exist.

enabled.description: Noise-carved caves. OFF by default: they cost more than everything else in the generator combined (the noise must be evaluated for every voxel of rock in the world), and they give you no control over where a system is or where it goes.  is the controllable, far cheaper mechanism. Turn this on for a deliberately honeycombed world.

threshold.description: Higher = wider, more connected tunnel network.

minDepth.description: Tunnels stay at least this far below the surface (no random pits in a meadow).

sampleStep.description: World units between cave-noise samples; values between them are smoothly interpolated. Cave noise is evaluated across most of a cell's VOLUME, which makes this the single biggest cost lever in the generator — doubling it is close to an 8x saving. Tunnels are tens of metres across, so 4 costs nothing visible; approach the voxel size only if you want genuinely rough cave walls.

entrances.description: Cave MOUTHS. Without this, `minDepth` holds everywhere and the network is sealed — a cave system nobody can enter. Relaxing the depth requirement on steep ground opens tunnels onto cliff faces and mountainsides, which is both where entrances belong and where they read as deliberate.

contrast.description: Spreads the climate noise across the full 0..1 range. WITHOUT it the documented semantics are a lie: raw fBm clusters hard around the middle (measured 0.23..0.65 for temperature), so a biome window written in honest 0..1 terms — a desert at moisture below 0.3, say — simply never fires and the biome silently does not exist anywhere in the world. 1 disables the spread.

edge.description: Border raggedness. Without it every biome boundary is an iso-contour of a smooth low-frequency noise field, which is exactly as artificial as it sounds — a clean arc of blight sweeping across a meadow. Set `warp` and `strength` to 0 for the old razor-smooth behaviour.

zones.description: Cut the world into large single-purpose regions. When set, temperature and moisture come from each zone's anchor (blended only across borders) instead of from the `temperature`/`moisture` noise, and every anchor carries landform multipliers so a mountain zone HAS mountains and a swamp is flat. The noise fields above still add `edge.strength` speckle. Omit for the classic noise climate.

lapseRate.description: Temperature (0..1) lost per world unit of altitude above sea level. Keep it SMALL. At 0.006 a 50 m hill is already 0.3 colder than the shore, which drops it straight into the polar band and puts snow on modest green hills — the classic symptom is a white hillside next to a meadow at the same latitude. Snow on genuine peaks is the `alpine` biome's height window doing its job; this only tilts the odds.

surfaces.description: The world's surface PALETTE, up to eight, blended per-vertex. Index order is the weight vector's order. Every biome names its cover as weights over this one palette, which is how a blighted zone can be all blighted-grass and no grass while a coast is sand and dirt: the weights it does not want are simply zero. Each extra surface costs three more fragment fetches (sampling is triplanar), so add them deliberately.

patches.description: Local surface variation layered over the biome result, in order — dirt worn through grass, rock breaking a desert, mottled blight. Biomes decide the KIND of place; patches keep it from being a flat sheet of one texture.

prefab.description: Prefab asset id to instance (preferred — keeps chunk docs collapsed).

model.description: Model asset id, when there is no prefab worth authoring.

foliageNormals.description: Passed to the emitted mesh: shade this model's alpha-cutout parts as a sphere. Set it on anything with leaf cards, or the canopy lights per-card — one plate blown out, the next black. See the mesh component's own field for why.

foliageUp.description: Passed to the emitted mesh: how far the reshaped leaf normals lean toward straight up. 1 shades them exactly like the grass cover.

brightness.description: Passed to the emitted mesh: multiply this model's base colour. See the mesh component's own field.

wind.description: Passed to the emitted mesh: vertex-shader wind. `sway` for bushes (bends from a base pinned to the ground), `ripple` for trees (leaf cards shimmer, trunk holds still). See the mesh component's own field.

cameraFade.description: Passed to the emitted mesh: dissolve this prop when it blocks the third-person camera's view of the character. Worth it on anything with leaf cards a player will walk into. See the mesh component's field.

biomes.description: Biome ids this may appear in; empty = anywhere.

biomeDensity.description: Per-biome thinning, biome id -> fraction of `density` that survives there (absent = 1, the full density). This is how ONE rule is a forest in the forest and a copse in the meadow, instead of two rules that have to be kept in step. Capped at 1 for the same reason `clump.floor` is: `density` fixes the lattice before any of this runs, so it is the PEAK and everything else thins it. A biome not in `biomes` at all is still excluded outright — this only grades the ones that are in.

clump.description: Gather this rule into groves/thickets with open ground between, instead of spreading it evenly over every biome it is allowed in. See the schema — this is the difference between a forest and an orchard.

density.description: Expected instances per square world unit. 0.01 = one per 10x10m, i.e. a light forest.

slopeMax.description: Steepest ground it will stand on.

slopeMin.description: Shallowest ground it will stand on, in the same sin(angle) units as slopeMax (0.71 = 45 degrees, 0.87 = 60). Raise it to make a rule STEEP-ONLY — scree, cliff rock, ledge growth — instead of the usual 'anywhere flat enough'.

yawOffset.description: Radians added to every instance's yaw. The fix for a model whose front does not face +Z: cliff rocks turn their +Z out of the face, so a model authored facing -Z needs Math.PI here.

cliff.description: Turn this rule into a CLIFF FACE rule: instead of one prop standing on the ground, it emits a vertical STACK of props bedded into the face below the clifftop. This is how a sheer voxel face stops reading as a painted texture and starts reading as rock. Pair it with a high `slopeMin` — a stack on gentle ground is just a tower of floating boulders.

height.description: World-Y window the ground must fall in.

alignToNormal.description: 0 = always upright, 1 = fully laid onto the slope.

yOffset.description: Sink (negative) or lift the instance along its own up axis.

jitter.description: How far off its lattice point each instance may wander.

clearance.description: Metres kept clear of every feature's EDGE — a path's shoulder, a river's bank foot, a town's radius, a monolith's footprint. 0 lets the rule stand props on a footpath, which is never wanted.

footprint.description: Radius of the prop's own ground footprint in MODEL units (scaled per instance). Two props are placed no closer than the SUM of their footprints plus `spacing`, and rules are solved largest-footprint first so big things claim ground before small ones fill in around them. 0 = derive from colliderSize.

spacing.description: Extra clear ground kept between this prop and any other, in world units.

lod.description: Passed to the emitted mesh: swap to a cheap distance proxy past ~100m. Turn it OFF for a model that is already cheap. Without a baked impostor the far tier is a BOX for a squat prop, so a 170-triangle rock spends the whole middle distance as a brown box — the proxy saves 150 triangles and costs you the rock. See the mesh component's own field.

pipeline.description: Stage name -> ISO timestamp of the last time it ran, stamped automatically whenever a worldgen stage writes the recipe. A world is built by a dozen stages that depend on each other, and half of them are an agent's job rather than a generator's; this is what lets `worldgen status` say which are done, which went STALE because something they depend on was re-run after them, and which have never run at all.

regions.description: The ZONES players and servers know by name — agent-drawn polygons with a story and a hub, borders on landmarks. Coarse (minutes to cross), not biomes, not the climate cells. Chat 'zone' lines and cluster placement read them; docs/world-editing/zones.md is the authoring procedure.

width.description: Full channel width at the bed.

widths.description: Per-point channel width, same length as `points`, overriding `width` along the channel: a river that widens as tributaries join and swells around its bends. `width` must still be the WIDEST of them (it sizes the carve's reach and the bank). `worldgen rivers` writes both.

depth.description: How far below the surrounding land the bed sits.

depths.description: Per-point channel depth, same length as `points`, overriding `depth` along the channel: a stream a metre deep at its head that is six metres deep where it meets the sea. The water surface sits 0.7 of the local depth over the bed. `depth` must still be the DEEPEST. `worldgen rivers` writes both.

bank.description: Extra distance over which the banks ease back up to natural terrain, at the channel's WIDEST; where `widths` are given the local bank is min(bank, 0.7 × local width + 3).

bedY.description: Per-point bed height, same length as `points`. OMIT IT when writing a river by hand: the field solves a descending bed through the points from the ground they cross (a channel depth under it, capped at a lake's level from the first point under a lake, running-min from the head so a ridge in the way is cut, the mouth a hair under the sea or flush with the river it ends on), and the world carves, banks and waters it live. `worldgen rivers --trace` writes one; a hand-written doc never should.

maxGrade.description: Steepest bed grade the SOLVED bed may carry (rise over run; 0.05 is 5 %), applied only when `bedY` is omitted. Where the ground drops faster — a coastal scarp, a lake's spill — the bed upstream is cut down to keep the grade, so the river reaches the sea through a gorge instead of sliding down the cliff as a tilted sheet. Not applied inside a lake: an outlet leaves flush with its lake and cascades from there. A water sheet reads as a river under about 2 %, as rapids to 5 %; 0 disables the limit.

water.description: Emit a water surface along the channel (a ribbon at bed + most of `depth`, in the recipe's `riverMaterial`). false is a dry gully: carved and painted, no sheet.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME painted on the bed and banks, so ground cover stops at the water: a channel cut through grassland is still grass to the splat otherwise, and the grass billboards grow in the river. Empty string leaves the biome's cover.

surfaceEdge.description: World units over which the bed surface fades into the bank.

taper.description: Metres over which the channel grows from a trickle to full width and depth at its HEAD. Without it a river begins at full size in the middle of a field, which is the single most obvious tell of a traced channel; with it the source reads as a stream forming.

ridges.description: Terrain raised along a polyline — barriers on the zone borders that had none. Written by `worldgen barriers` (ids `barrier-*`, rewritten on every run); hand-written ridges are kept.

shoulder.description: Distance over which the cut/fill eases back into natural terrain.

smooth.description: Metres BEYOND the shoulder over which the ground is regraded into a smooth embankment: from the road edge out to `shoulder + smooth`, the natural terrain is replaced by a clean slope from the road surface to `leftY`/`rightY` and only fades back into the rough ground at the outer edge. Without it the shoulder merely blends the road height into whatever crinkle is there, and a road across noisy ground reads as a notch in jagged terrain. Needs `leftY`/`rightY`; `worldgen roads` writes all three.

leftY.description: Per-point ground height at the outer edge of the `smooth` band on the road's left (positive cross-product side).

rightY.description: Per-point ground height at the outer edge of the `smooth` band on the road's right.

flatten.description: How completely the road height wins over natural terrain.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME painted along the roadway, overriding whatever the biome would put there. A road that only flattens the ground is invisible from the air — grass graded flat still reads as grass. Set to an empty string to leave the biome's own cover in place (a paved street in a town, say).

surfaceEdge.description: World units over which the painted surface fades into the surrounding ground. The verge.

surfaceByBiome.description: Palette surface NAME to paint instead of `surface` where a given biome (by id) holds the ground — `{ alpine: "gravel" }` makes a footpath gravel across the snow and dirt everywhere else. Blended by biome membership, so the swap fades across the biome boundary. `worldgen paths`/`trails` write gravel for every snow-dominant biome when the palette has gravel.

excludeScatter.description: When omitted or true, exclude scatter and ground cover across the whole town pad. Set false for landscaped towns whose roads and building foundations provide local clearances.

tier.description: How big a place this is. It sets the pad's size and, later, what gets built on it; `worldgen towns` buckets a world into a few capitals on the coast, some cities, and a long tail of villages and hamlets, because a world of forty identical 45 m discs reads as forty identical places. Absent on a recipe written before tiers existed — read it as "capital" when `tags` says so, "town" otherwise.

falloff.description: Distance beyond `radius` over which the pad blends into natural terrain.

flatten.description: How hard the whole footprint is pulled to `groundY`. 1 is a table top. A TERRACED town sets this to 0 and leaves the hill alone — its `terraces` are the flat ground, and the slope between them is the point.

terraces.description: Shelves stepped up the site, for a town with verticality. Written by `worldgen terrace`, which also cuts the ramps between them as ordinary roads (`<town>-ramp-*`). Empty for a town on the flat.

gates.description: Ways in. A town with gates is entered ONLY through them: `worldgen paths` and `worldgen trails` route to the gate mouth that faces where they come from instead of to the centre, and the pad is a wall to every route not arriving at one. Leave empty for an open village whose lanes are the road.

lakes.description: Standing water at its own level, basin carved beneath. Written by `worldgen rivers`.

bridges.description: Road decks spanning rivers. Written by `worldgen roads`.

fills.description: Sediment-filled hollows on the river network. Written by `worldgen rivers`.

riverPaths.description: Hand- or agent-drawn river centrelines. AUTHORING input: `worldgen rivers` solves each into `rivers`.

tunnels.description: Carved cave passages. Written by `worldgen caves`.

height.description: 0 = a sphere. Above 0 the blob is a VERTICAL CAPSULE this tall, rising from `center` — which is what turns the escape hatch into a monolith: a desert pillar is one line of JSON rather than a stack of spheres, and it stays one line when you drag it somewhere else.

topRadius.description: Radius at the TOP of a capsule (needs `height`). Omit for a uniform column. A value below `radius` is what turns a pillar into a needle — a spire tapering as it rises reads as weathered stone, a cylinder reads as a prop.

name.description: What players call this one — 'The Warren Mouth'. Set by a story; a bare generated POI has none and is labelled by its id.

zone.description: Region id this POI stands in (recipe `regions`), or empty in an unzoned world. Stamped by `worldgen pois` and re-stamped whenever the zones are redrawn, so a zone's contents can be listed, dressed and quested over without anything having to re-run point-in-polygon over 1000 landmarks.

radius.description: Area of effect for kinds that have one — a waystation's sanctuary circle (metres).

tags.description: Free-form; "safe" marks a sanctuary (no player-on-player damage within `radius`), "pass" a zone-border pass.

camps.description: Enemy camps — where monsters live. Written by `worldgen spawn`, which also patches the matching spawnArea entities into the scene (ids `camp-*`, rewritten on every run); hand-written camps are kept.

verticalRange.description: The vertical band actually meshed per cell. A voxel world is not infinite in Y for free.

textureFilter.description: Magnification filter for every terrain surface texture. Set 'nearest' for PIXEL ART so it stays chunky instead of being smeared smooth up close. Emitted onto the terrain material by `worldgen material`.

macroNoise.description: Noise multiplied over the whole blended terrain to break up texture repetition, emitted onto the terrain material by `worldgen material`. It lives HERE and not only in the material because the material is derived data — anything written straight into it is lost the next time the palette changes and it gets re-emitted.

waterMaterial.description: Material asset id for river ribbons and lake sheets emitted into streamed cells. Without it rivers are carved but dry. `worldgen init` writes one beside the terrain material.

riverMaterial.description: Material asset id for river ribbons specifically — a water material with `flowMode: "channel"`, so the water visibly runs downstream. Falls back to `waterMaterial` (standing water). `worldgen rivers` writes `<waterMaterial>-river` and sets this.

bridgeMaterial.description: Material asset id for the placeholder decks emitted for `features.bridges`. `worldgen roads` writes a plain timber-coloured one when the recipe has none.

oceanFloor.description: Ground height far out to sea, well below seaLevel so open water is unmistakably water. Keep it above `minY` or the sea bed falls through the world's solid floor.

landFloor.description: Metres above seaLevel that the INTERIOR of a landmass is held at or above. Above 0 this switches the continent from a height blend to a shore PROFILE: the ground rises from oceanFloor to this floor across the coast band and the terrain's own relief fades in on top of it, so the coastline is exactly the warped outline of the continent and nowhere else. That is what keeps the ocean from bleeding into every inland dip — with the interior held above the sea, standing water inland is only ever a LAKE at its own level. 0 = the legacy blend (inland hollows below seaLevel fill with ocean).

shelf.description: Where in the coast band (0 = open sea, 1 = inland) the shoreline sits when `landFloor` is set. Lower = more of the band is beach and shallows.

limit.description: THE WORLD BOUNDARY: distance from the origin beyond which everything is open ocean at oceanFloor, whatever the continents say. Streaming skips cells past it, the ocean plane is sized to it, and nothing is placed beyond it. Omit for no hard edge.

limitFalloff.description: Metres over which land is pulled under approaching `limit`.

center.description: World-space XZ centre of the landmass.

radius.description: Distance from the centre that is solidly inland — the terrain here is whatever the noise bands make it.

falloff.description: Width of the band over which land descends to the ocean floor. The coastline sits inside it, so a WIDE falloff gives beaches and shallow bays and a narrow one gives sea cliffs. Mountains caught in this band are compressed rather than clipped, which is what puts lowlands around the rim instead of peaks meeting the water.

warp.description: Coastline raggedness as a fraction of `falloff`: 0 is a clean arc, ~0.6 gives peninsulas, headlands and bays. Above 1 the coast breaks into islands.

warpScale.description: Metres per lobe of coastline wobble. Small values fray the coast into inlets; large ones bend the whole landmass.

coastVariation.description: How much `falloff` varies around the coast, as a fraction. 0.6 means some stretches of shore descend over 40% of the band (steep: headlands and sea cliffs) and others over 160% (gentle: beaches and shallow bays). This is what gives one island a beach on one side and cliffs on the other.

coastVariationScale.description: Metres per cycle of the falloff variation — how long a stretch of cliff or beach coast is.

lobes.description: Extra discs [dx, dz, radius], relative to `center`, smoothly UNIONED with the main one. This is what stops a continent being a circle: two or three lobes make a crescent, an L, a landmass with a peninsula and a gulf. Each lobe still gives an exact distance to its shore, so the shore profile and the land floor hold everywhere.

lobeBlend.description: Metres over which lobes merge into one another instead of meeting at a crease. Wider = softer bays where they join.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.0008 = continents, 0.01 = hills, 0.08 = rocks.

amplitude.description: World units this band contributes (ridged bands run 0..amplitude, others +/-amplitude).

ridged.description: Sharp crests, flat valleys — the difference between rolling hills and a mountain range.

seed.description: Added to the world seed so two identically-tuned bands still differ.

erosion.description: Slope-weighted octaves: fine detail is damped where the band is already steep, so valleys come out smooth and walkable while ridgelines stay crisp. This is the single biggest lever against terrain that reads as jagged noise — plain fBm puts the same 30 m crinkle on every slope in the world. 0.3-0.6 on the mountain band; costs ~40% more per octave (derivative noise).

crest.description: Ridged bands only: round the crests. The ridged fold puts a knife-edge crease at every ridgeline and summit of every octave, and the voxel mesh renders each one as a corner it cannot smooth — the 'cliffs that come to a sharp edge at the top'. 0 (default) keeps the crease; 0.2 rounds each crest over about a fifth of the band's swing without moving the summit line. Free.

cliff.description: How much steeper the land gets at the waterline where the coast noise says 'rugged'. 0 makes every shore a beach, which is the failure this fixes: a height-band beach rule applied to a uniformly gentle coastline rings the entire world in one unbroken strip of sand.

band.description: World units above and below sea level the steepening reaches. Roughly the height of the headlands.

frequency.description: How often the coast alternates between cliff and cove.

amplitude.description: World units of dune crest. 0 disables the band entirely, and with it the extra climate lookup per column.

stretch.description: Elongation across the prevailing wind. 1 is lumps; 3-4 is the long parallel ridges that read as sand.

angle.description: Wind direction in radians — the axis the ridges run along.

amplitude.description: World units of table height. 0 disables the band.

steps.description: Strata per table: each is a riser and a tread.

sharpness.description: How square the risers are. 0 is a smooth dome.

height.description: The highest the ground can be, asymptotically. Peaks approach it and never reach it.

softness.description: Metres below `height` at which the compression begins. Wider = gentler summits.

step.description: Metres of altitude per terrace — the height of one riser, and roughly the height of one cliff band.

sharpness.description: How square the riser is. 0 leaves the slope untouched; 0.72 spends ~28% of each band's altitude on the riser and flattens the rest into a tread. Past ~0.9 the riser is vertical enough that the voxel lattice, not this number, is what limits it.

strength.description: How much of the terraced profile to blend in where the mask is full. Below 1 the risers soften back toward the raw slope.

rounding.description: Fraction of each riser's height spent easing into the tread at its top and foot, instead of meeting it at a crease. 0 is the raw clamp — a riser that hits the tread at a corner, which the mesh renders as a knife edge along every cliff top. 0.25 rounds the crest and the foot over a quarter of the riser each while the middle half stays as sheer as `sharpness` asks.

minBands.description: How many `step` bands of mountain relief a place must have before it is terraced at all, fading in over the next 1.4 bands. This is what keeps cliffs ON MOUNTAINS: without it the edge of the mountain band — a hillock with one band's worth of height — gets a single enormous step, which reads far harsher than the mountain itself does because there is no mountain around it to explain it, and it is visible from a long way off.

mask.description: WHERE the terracing happens. Without this every mountain in the world is terraced from base to summit and reads as a ziggurat, which is not what a mountain range looks like — a range is mostly smooth flank with cliff bands breaking out of it here and there. Widen the start..end gap for cliffs that fade in; raise `start` for rarer, more dramatic ones.

jitter.description: Metres the band boundaries wander from place to place. Without it every terrace in the world is a perfectly level contour ring at the same altitude, which reads as a contour map rather than as rock.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.0012 is a cliff band a few hundred metres across.

start.description: Mask value at which terracing begins to appear.

end.description: Mask value at which it is in full.

strength.description: World units the surface can bulge horizontally. 0 = a pure heightfield.

slopeStart.description: Only steep ground gets overhangs — flat fields must stay walkable.
Steepness at which the tunnel network may start reaching the surface.

slopeEnd.description: Steepness at which it fully may.

minDepth.description: The `minDepth` that applies on fully steep ground. NEGATIVE means tunnels are allowed to push past the surface, which is what actually cuts an opening; at 0 they only ever kiss it.

warp.description: World units the climate field is domain-warped by before it is read. This is the LARGE-scale raggedness: it makes a desert reach a peninsula into the meadow instead of ending on a smooth curve.

strength.description: Fine noise (in the climate's own 0..1 units) added to temperature and moisture. This is the SMALL-scale raggedness: it breaks the last few metres of every border into speckle, so the transition is a scatter of blighted ground in the grass rather than a line.

heightJitter.description: World units of noise added to the ground height that HEIGHT windows are tested against — the same trick for the snowline and the beach, which are height-driven rather than climate-driven.

size.description: Mean zone diameter in metres. A region should take minutes to cross, not seconds.

jitter.description: How far each zone's site wanders from its grid point. 0 is a checkerboard.

warp.description: Metres the zone borders are pushed around by noise, so they read as coastlines rather than as cell walls.

border.description: Width of the blend between two zones, in metres. Biome rules still see a gradient across it.

strength.description: How strongly zones sort by latitude. 0 = anchors are picked by weight alone.

scale.description: Metres from the cold pole to the hot one, centred on the origin along `axis`.

seed.description: Added to the world seed for the zone layout alone, so the layout can be re-rolled without moving a single hill. Which anchor a zone gets is a draw, and a small world can draw no desert at all: a generator that needs every kind of place can sweep this until each anchor covers real land.

weight.description: How often zones pick this anchor, relative to the others.

latitude.description: Preferred latitude band, 0 = the cold pole, 1 = the hot pole (see `climate.zones.latitude`). A zone picks anchors by weight TIMES how close its own latitude is to this, so tundra collects at one end of the world and jungle at the other instead of both being sprinkled everywhere. Omit = anywhere.

relief.description: Multiplies the MOUNTAIN band here. 1 = a mountain zone; 0 = no peaks at all.

hills.description: Multiplies the hills band. 0 = a plain; 1.5 = broken country.

dunes.description: Multiplies the dune band (`terrain.dunes`) here. 1 = a dune sea.

mesas.description: Multiplies the mesa band (`terrain.mesas`) here. 1 = badlands: terraced tables and buttes.

flatten.description: Pulls the continent band down toward the land floor. 1 = a low, level plain hugging the waterline — swamp ground.

name.description: Human/AI-facing label: grass, sand, rock, snow.

color.description: Tint, and the whole appearance until a texture is supplied.

map.description: Texture asset id (assets/textures/) — albedo, projected triplanar.

blend.description: Softness of the temperature/moisture/slope window edges, in those windows' own 0..1 units.

heightBlend.description: Softness of the `height` window edges, in WORLD UNITS — height is the one window measured in metres, so it needs its own blend or a 0.08 softness makes a razor edge across a hillside.

weight.description: Relative pull where several rules match equally.

cliffStart.description: Steepness at which `cliff` starts replacing `surface`, in sin(angle). 0.57 is 35 degrees, roughly the angle of repose: past it soil and sand stop staying put, which is why cover gives way to rock there. These are authored against `slope()` units, so anything that measures steepness differently silently means a different ANGLE here.

cliffEnd.description: Steepness at which `cliff` fully replaces `surface`. 0.82 is 55 degrees.

tint.description: Multiplied over the blended surface color — cheap per-biome variation.

zones.description: Zone anchor ids (`climate.zones.anchors[].id`) this rule belongs to. The rule's membership is multiplied by the blended zone weight, so a rule listed here exists ONLY inside those zones — which is how a blighted region and a badland can both be hot-and-dry without fighting over the same climate corner. Omit for a rule that applies wherever its climate/height/slope windows say.

label.description: Does this rule NAME the place? Cover-only rules — a crag rule that paints bare rock on steep ground in every biome — must set false. `biome().id` is the strongest rule by membership, and everything that asks 'which biome is this' reads it: scatter's `biomes` filter above all. A cover rule left labelling quietly renames every slope in the world, and the pines filtered to "meadow" stop appearing on hills.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME to lay down (matched case-insensitively).

biomes.description: Biome ids this may appear in; empty = anywhere. The gate is the biome's blended membership, so patches fade out across a border instead of stopping at it.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.02 ~ 50 m blotches.

threshold.description: Noise level (-1..1) at which the patch starts. Higher = rarer, smaller patches.

blend.description: Noise range over which it fades in. Small = hard-edged scabs, large = soft mottling.

strength.description: How completely the patch replaces the ground under it at full mask. 1 = bare.

slope.description: Restrict to a steepness window — dirt worn through on flat ground, scree only on slopes.

mode.description: Two different motions, not one with a knob. `sway` BENDS the whole plant from a base pinned to the ground - displacement grows with height, so it leans as one piece. That is a bush or a reed. `ripple` shivers each leaf card on the spot with NO net lean, phase varying across the model so cards move against each other: the canopy shimmers while the tree stands still, which is what real timber does in a light wind. Putting `sway` on a tree is the classic mistake - the trunk swings like a blade of grass and the model reads as rubber.

strength.description: Peak displacement in METRES of world space, not a fraction of the model. A ripple wants 0.02-0.06; a bush sway 0.08-0.2.

canopy.description: `ripple` only: fraction of the model height where the canopy starts. Everything below is held perfectly still, which is how the trunk stays out of it. It is a HEIGHT test rather than a 'is this the leaf material' test on purpose: Blockbench exports every material as alphaMode MASK, so a cutout test catches the trunk too (the same trap `foliageNormals` documents), while height does not care where the trunk sits horizontally.

materials.description: Only move materials whose NAME, or whose colour texture's name, contains one of these (case-insensitive, COMMA-SEPARATED) — `leaves` for a model whose leaf texture is called Leaves, `leaves,bush` for one rule that covers a whole shelf of props whatever each model calls its own foliage sheet. The rest of the model stands still and the `canopy` height test is skipped, so the trunk stays put by NAME rather than by height. Name the texture or material in the DCC tool before export: Blockbench exports a pasted texture as literally 'pasted', which matches nothing, and an unmatched model gets no wind at all (`split-gltf.mjs --texnames` names them after the fact).

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit — the size of one grove. 0.004 ~ 250 m stands, 0.02 ~ 50 m thickets.

threshold.description: Noise level (-1..1) at which the clump starts. Higher = rarer, smaller, further-apart clumps.

blend.description: Noise range over which it fades in. Small = a hard treeline, large = a stand that thins out at its edge.

floor.description: Fraction of the density that survives OUTSIDE the clumps. 0 = real clearings you can walk across; 0.15 = a thinned scatter between the stands, which is what most woodland actually looks like.

seed.description: Added to the world seed, so two rules with identical settings clump in different places.

stack.description: How many props down one column, picked per lattice point. The stack stops early where the face does.

spacing.description: Metres of drop between one prop and the next. Set it under the model's height so they overlap and read as one mass.

spacingJitter.description: How much each step may vary, as a fraction of `spacing`.

embed.description: Depth pushed INTO the face along its inward normal, in MODEL units — it is multiplied by the instance scale, like `yOffset`, so resizing a prop does not leave it hanging off the wall. This is the field that decides whether the prop looks bolted onto the cliff or part of it; roughly a third of the model's depth is a good start.

embedJitter.description: Random variation on `embed`, in the same model units.

lateral.description: Metres each prop may slide sideways along the face, so a column is not a plumb line of rocks.

faceOut.description: How strongly each prop turns to face out of the cliff. 1 = square to the face, 0 = free yaw (the ordinary scatter behaviour).

yawSpread.description: Radians of random yaw either side of the outward direction. This plus `tilt` is what stops a stack looking like one model copy-pasted.

tilt.description: Radians of random tilt off vertical, about a random horizontal axis.

lean.description: Radians the prop tips BACK into the face (negative tips it out). A cliff recedes as it rises, so an upright prop bedded at its base has its top hanging in open air — which is exactly what makes a face read as planted menhirs instead of rock. Roughly `atan(model height / (2 x embed))` cancels it. This is NOT `alignToNormal`: that one lays a prop ONTO a slope, which on a cliff leans it further out.

minDrop.description: The face must fall at least this far below the lattice point for the column to start at all. Guards against decorating every short steep bank in the world.

search.description: Metres to march outward looking for the face at each step's height. Wider catches gentler faces, and it is the per-instance cost knob — but it is also how far a prop can end up from the lattice point that owns it, so keep it WELL under a quarter of `cellSize` or a cell starts emitting props that live in its neighbour and pop when it unloads.

id.description: Stable slug, referenced by chat, placement and stories. Never rename one players have seen.

name.description: What players see: 'Ashfall Canyon', 'The Hollow Vale'.

story.description: Two to five sentences: what this place is, why anyone goes there, what is wrong with it. The seed the AI dungeon master grows consequences from; also the tooltip text on the map.

polygon.description: Border in world metres [x, z], clockwise or counter-clockwise, no self-crossing. Follow LANDMARKS a player cannot see across — ridge lines, river centrelines, gorge rims, the coast — never a straight line over open ground: the border is where a server swap can happen, and a swap must not show two worlds.

hub.description: Where an arriving player is placed and the map labels the region — normally a town centre inside the polygon.

landmarks.description: Feature ids inside or bounding the region (towns, rivers, canyons, peaks, pois) — what its borders were drawn on.

level.description: Intended character level band [min, max]; the spawn tables and the story pitch to it.

cap.description: Players per server copy of this region before another copy opens. Omit = the cluster default.

within.description: Id of the region this one is CUT OUT of: wherever this polygon lies inside its parent, this region wins (regionAt prefers the nested zone). How a town is a zone of its own inside the wilderness around it — a simple polygon cannot hold a hole, so the cut-out is declared, not drawn. Never overlaps otherwise.

tags.description: "town" marks a town zone (hub = the town centre, landmarks[0] = its town id); "safe" makes the whole zone a sanctuary; "draft" = placeholder from worldgen zones.

__schema164.description: World-space XZ control points; the feature is the polyline through them.

depth.description: How far below the surrounding land the floor sits.

rim.description: Horizontal distance the walls take to climb back to natural terrain.

steps.description: Terraces in each wall. 1 is a smooth ramp; 3-4 reads as bedded rock.

stepSharpness.description: 0 = the terraces vanish into a straight slope, 1 = vertical risers and flat treads.

height.description: Metres the crest stands ABOVE the natural terrain.

falloff.description: Horizontal distance the flanks take to meet natural ground on either side of the crest.

heights.description: Per-point crest heights (one per point), overriding `height`. The barriers stage sets each so the crest sits `height` above the HIGHER flank measured `falloff` out — a 35 m ridge on a 30 m slope is a step, not a wall, unless it is measured that way.

tags.description: "barrier" plus "zone:<id>" for each zone it separates, when written by `worldgen barriers`.

points.description: World-space XZ centreline of the shelf; a single point is a round pad.

radius.description: Half-width of the flat shelf, measured from the centreline.

falloff.description: Distance beyond `radius` over which the shelf's height blends into what is around it — the step's face.

groundY.description: The shelf's height. Unlike a town pad this is never inferred: a terrace exists to be at a chosen level.

at.description: World XZ of the gate mouth — where the town's own roads end and the world's begin. Every path to this town arrives HERE, not at the centre.

facing.description: Outward XZ direction the road leaves in, pointing away from the town. Normalised on use; [0, 0] is an error.

width.description: Clear width of the opening. A path arriving here is drawn no wider than this.

approach.description: Metres of DEAD STRAIGHT path laid outward from `at` along `facing` before the router takes over. This is what makes the road leave square-on through the arch instead of raking past it; 0 lets the router start bending at the gate itself.

polygon.description: World-space XZ outline of the shore. Omit for a disc of `radius` about `center`.

waterY.description: Surface height. The basin is carved to sit below it; land outside the outline is untouched past `bank`.

depth.description: How far below the surface the deepest water is.

bank.description: Distance over which the shore eases from the waterline back to natural terrain, and the bed from the shore down to `depth`.

carve.description: true (hand-placed lakes): dig the basin — everything inside the outline goes down to `depth`, and a `bank` outside it eases to the waterline, whatever the ground was. false (`worldgen rivers` writes this): the terrain already holds the basin the hydrology found, so only ground at or under the surface is deepened, blended over two banks, and ground standing over a metre above it — an island, or an outline that overshot onto a hillside — is left alone. Carving a traced outline dug craters with vertical walls where it strayed uphill.

material.description: Water material for THIS lake, overriding the recipe's `waterMaterial`. A swamp pool is still, murky and opaque; a tarn is clear — one water for both reads wrong in both.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME painted on the bed and a `shore` band around the outline — wet sand, gravel — so the ground under and beside the water is not the biome's grass. Empty leaves the biome's cover; an unknown name paints nothing.

shore.description: Metres beyond the outline the `surface` fades out over.

points.description: World-space XZ of the two abutments: where the road stops on one bank and resumes on the other.

deckY.description: Height of the deck surface; the roads on both banks end at this height.

waterY.description: Water surface under the span, for the WFC stage to size piers.

material.description: Material for the deck, overriding the recipe's `bridgeMaterial`.

polygon.description: World-space XZ outline of the hollow.

y.description: Height the floor is raised to: the hollow's spill level, a little over.

bank.description: Distance beyond the outline over which the raise eases out.

points.description: World-space XZ, head first, mouth last.

width.description: Channel width at the mouth; the head is narrower unless `widths` are given.

points.description: World-space path in 3D — unlike rivers and roads, a cave goes up and down as well as along.

radius.description: Passage radius. Keep it comfortably ABOVE the world's voxel size (cellSize / resolution): marching cubes cannot represent a hole much narrower than one voxel, so a thinner tunnel is silently sealed in the mesh and in the collider cooked from it, however open the field says it is.

endRadius.description: Radius at the last point; omit for a uniform tube. Lets a passage open out into a chamber.

center.description: World-space XZ. Ground height is sampled from the field, so no Y is stored — the camp follows the terrain when it changes.

zone.description: Region id this camp sits in (recipe `regions`), or empty in an unzoned world. What a difficulty tier, a faction or a story hook keys on.

area.description: The spawnArea component emitted onto the scene entity, verbatim.

tags.description: Free-form. `worldgen spawn` writes a distance tier ("near", "far") off the zone hub.

__schema249.description: Metres from the area's origin within which a player wakes it: the packs spawn the first time, resume afterwards.

__schema251.description: Once awake, the area sleeps only when no player is within this (hysteresis — keep it larger than radius).

__schema253.description: Seconds with no player inside sleepRadius before the pack is paused in place. It does not despawn: a returning player finds it where it was.

template.description: NPC template: the id of an npc-tagged scene subtree, or a name registered on the server at runtime.

spread.description: Metres around the origin the pack is scattered in (uniform disc).

__schema257.description: Metres from home an enemy may chase before it must turn back. Handed to each NPC's root script as the `leash` param (with `home`, `roam`, `spawnArea`); the server also fences at 1.5× as a backstop.

__schema259.description: Idle wander radius around home, passed as the `roam` param.

above.description: World units of air polygonized above the highest ground in a cell — headroom for overhangs and arches.

below.description: World units of rock polygonized below the lowest ground in a cell. This is what makes surface caves enterable, and it is THE vertical cost knob: it multiplies both the sampled volume AND the cave surface the mesher has to triangulate, so it hits twice. Deeper cave networks want vertical chunk sections, not a bigger band here.

scale.description: World units per cycle of the broad band.

strength.description: Brightness swing, plus and minus. 0 disables the whole overlay.

detailScale.description: Second band, near tile size (10-20). This is the one that hides the grid up close.

colorStrength.description: How far the overlay shifts COLOUR, per channel, on top of the brightness swing. Brightness alone makes a large area read as one material under uneven light; letting the channels drift apart slightly — warmer here, greyer there — is what reads as the ground actually being different from place to place. 0.06-0.15 is a natural mottle; past ~0.25 the terrain goes tie-dye.

colorScale.description: World units per cycle of the colour band. Defaults to `scale`. Set it larger for broad regional colour shifts that survive being seen from a distance.

warp.description: How far the texture PROJECTION is pushed around by noise before it is sampled, as a fraction of each layer's OWN tile, so one setting means the same thing to a 3.5m grass tile and a 9m cliff tile. This is the one that actually kills tiling: brightness noise can only shade OVER a grid, and the grid is still underneath it — on a big flat-lit face seen from a distance the eye finds it anyway. Warping the projection means neighbouring tiles no longer line up, so there is no grid left to find. 0.25-0.5 is usually enough; past about 0.6 the texture visibly smears.

warpScale.description: World units per cycle of the warp. Measured: keep it near TWICE the tile size, not far above it. A warp much coarser than the tile slides whole tiles around and leaves the motif inside each one perfectly intact, so a strongly patterned texture still reads as a pattern; a warp at roughly tile scale distorts the motif itself, which is what stops a big rock face looking stamped.

__schema1.description: Metres between lattice samples. A dungeon wants 0.2-0.3: fine enough that a 0.4 m step reads as a step, coarse enough to mesh in a second.

__schema3.description: World-space extent to mesh. Omit and it is derived from the nodes, which is what you want unless a node is deliberately unbounded.

__schema6.description: Surface names, index-for-index with the `terrain-splat` material's splat layers. Names are for humans; the indices are what the mesh carries.

__schema9.description: Default palette triple, used by any node that declares none.

__schema14.description: Applied IN ORDER over empty space. Later nodes win.

__schema17.description: `add` unions this shape into the solid, `sub` carves it out as air, `intersect` clips the solid to it.

__schema20.description: Prism footprint in local X/Z metres, extruded by height along Y. Simple non-self-intersecting boundary, either winding; concave outlines allowed. Do not repeat the closing vertex.

__schema28.description: Radius of a rounded edge on this primitive. 0 keeps the corner sharp, which is the whole reason to mesh a volume with dual contouring.

__schema30.description: Smooth-min radius against everything before it. 0 is a hard boolean; raise it where cut rock should melt into a natural cave.

__schema32.description: Palette indices this node paints. Omit to inherit the document default.

__schema33.description: Bounded two-frequency displacement of this primitive in local metres. Use on cave cuts; leave masonry cuts unperturbed. Disables distance-based block rejection.

__schema35.description: Required by, and only read by, `shape: "heightfield"`: the sampled surface this node thickens into a slab. Its footprint and thickness come from `size`.

__schema36.description: Heights sampled on a regular grid and thickened into a slab. The footprint is size[0] x size[2] in local X/Z centred on the origin, size[1] is the slab THICKNESS, and heights are bilinear between samples and clamped at the edges. Nothing outside the footprint is solid, so the node has a real boundary. Its distance field is an APPROXIMATION (exact under a flat patch, an under-estimate on a slope), which is why it disables distance-based block rejection the way `noise` does.

__schema37.description: Samples across local X, both edges included. Spacing is size[0]/(width-1) metres.

__schema38.description: Samples across local Z, both edges included. Spacing is size[2]/(depth-1) metres.

__schema39.description: width*depth heights in LOCAL metres, relative to the node's own origin. Row-major with X fastest: index 0 is the -x/-z corner, index width*depth-1 the +x/+z one. Either a plain number array or a base64 string of little-endian float32 of exactly that length — see `encodeHeightfieldValues`.

__schema42.description: Which side of the sampled surface the slab hangs on. `floor` is solid from h-size[1] up to h (ground you stand on); `ceiling` is solid from h up to h+size[1] (a vault you walk under).

__schema44.description: Required by shape mesh: closed indexed local triangle solids, unioned and sampled by the shared CSG/DC path. Node position/rotation apply; size is ignored. Triangle palette assignments remain repaintable with volume paint.

__schema45.description: Closed indexed triangle solids sampled as a CSG signed-distance field, then extracted by the shared dual-contouring mesh path. Geometry must be an embedded closed manifold; self-intersections are rejected with 1e-9 relative tolerance at shared edges/vertices. A 64-machine-epsilon coordinate-scale boundary band consistently counts exactly touching closed surfaces as solid; no voxel smoothing or lattice changes. No UVs or imported render mesh fallback.

__schema46.description: Flat local XYZ coordinates in metres, Y up. Every indexed vertex belongs to a closed surface; bake scale into coordinates. Node position/rotation transform these coordinates; size is ignored.

__schema48.description: Triangle vertex indices, three per triangle. Shared vertices must use shared indices within a solid. No zero-area triangles, open edges, nonmanifold vertices/edges, or inconsistent winding. A whole connected shell may have either winding.

__schema50.description: Triangle counts of consecutive closed solids; their sum must equal indices.length/3. Solids are UNIONED even when they overlap. Each solid owns disjoint vertex indices; touching solids may duplicate coordinates. Omit for one closed solid. Disconnected boundary shells within one solid use parity (for example a sealed cavity); overlapping solids must be separate ranges.

__schema53.description: One volume palette index per source triangle, in index order. Overrides this node's floor/wall/ceiling palette at its surface, including carved faces. Omit to inherit the node surface. Ordinary volume paint strokes apply afterward.

__schema55.description: Persistent ordered texture strokes, evaluated after the CSG surface palette.

items.description: Spherical texture stroke in volume-local metres. Smooth falloff; later strokes blend over earlier ones without changing density or collision.

__schema62.description: Optional local-space facing direction for an angle-limited area fill.

__schema64.description: Maximum angle in degrees from the chosen normal. 180 paints all facing directions.

__schema66.description: Uniform coverage inside radius instead of brush falloff. This is a bounded facing-angle fill, not a connected-component flood fill.

sheet.description: Spritesheet data-asset id. Its grid is the flipbook: columns are frames, rows are colour variants.

row.description: Sheet row. 5 is the greyscale variant in the purchased library — leave it and let `color` tint.

size.description: Metres — the quad's width; height follows `aspect`.

orient.description: billboard faces the camera; ground lies flat (marks, runes); vertical stands upright and yaws toward the camera (a slash, a wave); facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); velocity aligns with the anchor's motion.

spin.description: Radians/sec the quad turns in its own plane. Lying on the ground that is a yaw; standing up it is a roll around a horizontal axis, which reads wrong on most symbols — the symbol catalog says which may.

yaw.description: Fixed rotation around the facing axis, radians.

randomYaw.description: Roll `yaw` per play — cheap variety for repeated impacts.

cell.description: [col, row] of ONE sheet cell shown as a static SYMBOL (a sigil, a glyph, an arrow) instead of playing the sheet as a flipbook. `fps`/`loop` are ignored; the symbol lives for `duration` (0 = the phase, or 0.6 s).

orbit.description: Metres the quad circles the anchor at, around its up axis. 0 = sits on the anchor.

orbitSpeed.description: Radians/sec along the orbit; negative runs the other way.

orbitPhase.description: Starting angle on the orbit, radians (0 = in front of the anchor). `repeat.turn` advances it per copy.

emitter.description: The emitter, in the `particles` component's own vocabulary. colorStart/colorEnd are overridden by the module's `color`/`colorEnd` unless they are left white.

burst.description: Particles spawned the moment the module starts.

stream.description: Keep emitting at the emitter's `rate` for the module's duration — channels, trails, auras.

radius.description: Outer radius in metres at scale 1.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer. 0 = a filled disc (a rune, a portal floor).

orient.description: ground lies on the terrain; vertical stands upright yawed toward the camera; facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); billboard faces the camera.

expand.description: Scale at birth and at death: a shockwave runs 0.1 → 1, a rune holds 1 → 1. `sizeCurve` overrides.

soft.description: Edge softness. 0 is a hard band; 1 fades across the whole width.

texture.description: Texture asset id laid across the disc (a rune, a sigil). Omitted = a procedural soft band.

arc.description: Degrees of the disc that are drawn, centred on the spell direction: 360 is a full ring, 90 a wedge in front of the caster.

noise.description: Breaks the band with scrolling noise so it reads as energy rather than a drawn circle.

swirl.description: Spiral distortion strength — the portal look. 0 = none.

drape.description: Ground rings follow the terrain under them (needs the host's ground probe).

height.description: Vertical/billboard: metres above the anchor the centre sits.

style.description: energy = noisy fresnel rim (barriers, orbs, charge-ups); glass = clean thin rim (bubbles, wards); smoke = dense normal-blended body (a cloud, a void); wire = a lattice of noise lines (arcane cages).

fresnel.description: Rim power — higher is a thinner, brighter edge. 0 = flat.

noise.description: How much scrolling 3D noise breaks the surface.

dissolve.description: [[t, threshold]] — the surface burns away where noise < threshold. A curve 0 → 1 is a shell that dissolves as it dies; 1 → 0 is one that assembles.

squash.description: Vertical scale: a dome on the ground is ~0.6, a tall bubble 1.4.

radius.description: Base radius, metres.

topRadius.description: Radius at the far end. Omitted = same as `radius` (a pillar); 0 = a cone to a point.

orient.description: up = a pillar out of the ground; forward = a cone along the spell direction (breath, spray); down = hanging from the sky onto the anchor.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed along the axis; positive = base → far end.

edgeFade.description: Fade at the silhouette so the tube has no hard vertical edges.

capFade.description: Fraction of the height faded out at the base and at the far end.

length.description: Metres along the spell direction when there is no target (or `toTarget` is off).

toTarget.description: Span anchor → target when the frame has one.

core.description: Bright inner core as a fraction of width. 0 = none.

style.description: energy = soft noisy glow; laser = hard clean edge; plasma = fat writhing body.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed toward the far end, metres/sec.

jitter.description: Metres of sideways displacement per segment.

refreshHz.description: How often the path re-rolls — the flicker.

count.description: Independent strands, each with its own path — a channelled storm rather than one arc.

spread.description: count > 1: metres the far ends scatter around the target.

arc.description: line = anchor to target/direction; sky = strikes DOWN onto the anchor from `length` metres up; ground = crawls along the terrain outward from the anchor in a random direction.

intensityCurve.description: [[t, multiplier]]. Default is a flash: spike, then decay.

asset.description: Model asset id. Omitted = the procedural `primitive`.

primitive.description: Procedural bodies for when no model is given.

motion.description: drop = falls from `from` metres up and lands as the module ends; rise = comes up out of the ground; hover = bobs in place; orbit = circles the anchor; launch = flies up and away; forward = glides `from` metres along the spell direction (a projection, an afterimage).

from.description: drop: start height above the anchor; rise: depth below it. 0 = auto.

spread.description: count > 1: radius they scatter or orbit within.

tint.description: Colour the body with the palette; off keeps the asset's own material.

length.description: Seconds of history the ribbon covers.

radius.description: circle: radius; cone: reach; line: length. Metres.

windup.description: Seconds the fill takes to reach the rim — the clock the target reads.

hold.description: Seconds the volume stays live after the windup.

growFrom.description: Live volumes that GROW: scale at the start of the hold, reaching 1 at its end.

curtain.description: Height of the vertical curtain, metres. 0 = auto from radius.

rimOpacity.description: The rim is the only number a dodge is judged against — keep it the brightest part, but not blown out.

dash.description: Rim dashing, 0..1: 0 is a solid band, 0.5 draws dashes as long as their gaps — the PSX marker look.

height.description: Vertical extent the drape is clamped to — keep it equal to the hit test's `delivery.height`.

radius.description: Outer reach of the arc, metres.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer: near 1 a thin crescent, near 0 a fat cleave.

sweep.description: Degrees the arc covers, centred on the spell direction.

tilt.description: Roll of the cutting plane around the spell direction: 0 = a horizontal cleave, 90 = a vertical overhead chop, ±45 diagonal.

reverse.description: Sweep the other way (right-to-left for a cleave, bottom-to-top for a chop).

sweepTime.description: Fraction of the life the leading edge takes to cross the arc; the rest is the tail fading out.

tail.description: Length of the trailing fade behind the leading edge, as a fraction of the sweep.

height.description: Metres above the anchor the arc's centre sits (chest height for a cleave).

core.description: How bright the leading edge is, toward the glow colour.

strength.description: Metres of camera displacement felt by a camera at the effect.

range.description: Metres over which the shake fades out. A camera at the effect feels the full `strength`, one at `range` or further feels nothing (quadratic falloff between). 0 disables the falloff — every camera in the world shakes, which is almost never what you want.

__schema0.description: Stable key so a human tweak or an agent's note can name this module.

__schema2.description: The library preset this came from — provenance for tweak-and-regenerate, never read at runtime.

at.description: origin = where the spell resolves (the volume's centre, the impact point); caster = the casting body; target = the targeted body or point; path = the projectile in flight (travel phase); ground = origin projected onto the terrain.

socket.description: caster/target only: a named attach point — rightHand, leftHand, chest, head, feet — resolved by the host to a bone-socket entity under that body. A missing socket falls back to the body itself.

offset.description: metres in the anchor's own frame: x right, y up, z FORWARD along the spell direction.

follow.description: Keep tracking the anchor for the module's whole life (a hand mid-swing, a projectile in flight) instead of sampling it once at start.

__schema11.description: Seconds it lives. 0 = natural length (a flipbook's frames, a burst's longest particle) or, for sustained kinds, the phase length.

__schema15.description: Where colour fades toward over life, for kinds that fade (particles, trail, beam core).

__schema17.description: additive = light (nearly everything magical); normal = matter that occludes (smoke, a poison cloud).

__schema24.description: PSX look: quantise the procedural shading to this many cells across the shape (0 = off, 16–32 reads as pixel art). Rings, shells, columns and beams snap their noise and bands to the grid; masks and sprites switch to nearest filtering.

__schema26.description: Alpha steps (0 = smooth). 3–5 turns soft falloffs into hard bands — the other half of the PSX look.

__schema28.description: [[t, multiplier]] over life, on top of the module's own size.

__schema31.description: Play this module as a STEPPING sequence — spikes that erupt one after another along the strike, a column of circles, glyphs spread around the caster. The sequencer expands it into `count` copies; the audit counts them.

count.description: Copies played. 1 = the module plays once.

every.description: Seconds between copies — the STEP. Nothing tweens between them; each copy appears whole.

step.description: Metres each copy moves on from the last, in the spell frame (x right, y up, z forward): [0,0,1.4] marches spikes away from the caster, [0,0.5,0] stacks rings into a column.

turn.description: Degrees each copy is turned around the anchor's up axis relative to the last. With `step` [0,0,r] and turn 360/count the copies stand in a circle; on an orbiting sprite it advances the orbit phase instead.

alternate.description: Flip the spin (and a slash's tilt) on every other copy — a column of circles turning against each other.

scale.description: Size multiplier applied per copy: 0.85 tapers a stack, 1.3 steps a shockwave outward.

jitter.description: Metres of seeded horizontal scatter added to each copy.

spread.description: Half-angle, in degrees, that each particle's launch direction is randomised within — on ANY shape, unlike coneAngle. 0 fires every particle along `direction` in exact parallel, which is right for a jet and wrong for anything suspended: a box of specks all falling parallel reads as SNOW. 180 is a full sphere, the usual choice for dust hanging in the air.

turbulence.description: Strength of a smooth per-particle wander field, units/sec^2. This is what makes dust look airborne rather than falling — motes curl past each other instead of tracking straight lines. Pair it with `drag` so the wander stays a drift instead of accumulating into a drift-off.

turbulenceSpeed.description: How fast the wander field evolves. Low (~0.2) is a lazy indoor drift; high is agitated.

fadeIn.description: Fraction of each particle's life spent ramping up from nothing to `opacityStart`. Anything meant to already be there — dust, fog, embers — needs this: with 0 every particle POPS into existence at full strength, which is the single clearest tell that an ambient effect is being spawned at you.

radial.description: Aim each particle along the line from the emitter's centre to its own spawn point instead of along `direction`: out = an explosion (needs a sphere/box shape so there IS an offset); in = energy CONVERGING on the centre — the charge-up look, particles born on the shell and flying inward. `spread` still scatters around that line.

sprite.description: The procedural sprite used when no `texture` is given: soft = a radial falloff (smoke, glow); square = a hard-edged square with a one-texel fade (PSX sparks and rain); pixel = a chunky 6x6 blob with stepped alpha (retro embers, motes); flame = an 8x8 pixel-art flame tongue pointing up the screen (PSX fire); ring = a hollow annulus, which is what a splash on the ground actually looks like (pair it with `orient: ground` and a growing `sizeCurve`); streak = a vertical tapered line for rain and sparks (pair it with `orient: velocity`); noise = a torn, cloudy puff with real internal structure, for anything big and slow that would otherwise read as a smooth grey blob — dust banks, smoke fronts (give a noise puff some `spin`: the structure is only visible because it turns). Every sprite but soft is nearest-filtered, so its texels stay hard at any size.

filter.description: Magnification of a `texture` sheet. nearest keeps low-res pixel-art sheets hard-edged (the PSX look); linear smears them. The procedural sprites choose their own filtering and ignore this.

steps.description: PSX banding: colour, size and opacity change in this many hard jumps over a particle's life instead of gliding (each step shows the value at its middle). 0 = smooth. 3–5 is the retro look — a flame that goes white, orange, red, gone reads as 1998; one that fades through every shade in between does not.

snap.description: PSX grid snap, in metres: rendered positions snap to a world grid of this size and quad sizes to multiples of it (a living particle never snaps below one cell). The same wobble as PSX vertex precision. 0 = off. Size it to the effect — around a fifth of the particle size — or it reads as a lattice.

frameRate.description: PSX stepping: the simulation advances in whole ticks of 1/frameRate seconds, so particles jump rather than slide (billboards still face the camera every frame). 0 = every frame. 8–15 is the retro range; flames at 12, lazy smoke lower.

subUV.description: Play the texture as a SPRITE SHEET, per particle. A still sprite drifting is the clearest tell that an effect is dated — every modern smoke, fire or impact particle animates on its own clock.

softFade.description: Metres over which a particle fades as it approaches solid geometry. 0 = off. A quad slicing visibly into the ground is THE thing that reads as cheap, and nothing else fixes it. Costs a scene-depth read, so leave it off for effects that never touch a surface (sparks in mid-air) — and NEVER pair it with `orient: ground`, which lies a quad centimetres above the surface behind it: the fade then measures that gap and erases the whole thing, which looks exactly like the effect failing to spawn.

stretch.description: Stretch each particle along its own velocity, in seconds of travel. 0 = round. Sparks and debris read as DOTS without this — the streak is the motion.

orient.description: What each quad points at. camera = the usual billboard, always square to the viewer. velocity = the quad's long axis is locked to the particle's WORLD velocity and it spins about that axis to face the camera — the difference between rain that falls the way the wind blows and rain that tilts with wherever you happen to be looking, which is what camera+`stretch` gives you (that one rolls the billboard by the SCREEN-space velocity, so the streaks swing as you turn and never foreshorten). ground = laid flat in the XZ plane, facing up: splash rings, ripples, scorch marks. upright = billboard that turns about Y only, so a tall quad stays vertical when you look up — dust banks, distant haze.

sizeCurve.description: [[t, size], …] over normalized life, overriding sizeStart/sizeEnd. A two-point lerp cannot describe a flash — spike, fast falloff, long dim tail — which is most of what separates an impact from a fading blob.

opacityCurve.description: [[t, opacity], …] over normalized life, overriding opacityStart/End and fadeIn.

space.description: world = particles trail behind a moving emitter; local = they ride it.

ground.description: Terrain contact. The host answers 'how high is the ground here' from the streamed terrain, sampled once per particle at birth; a particle that falls to it dies or settles. Terrain only — props, roofs and water are not tested. Needs space: world. Settled particles count toward `max`, so a settling snowfall wants a large one.

mode.description: life = play the sheet once across the particle's lifetime (smoke that billows and dissipates); loop = play it repeatedly at `fps`; random = hold one frame chosen per particle, which is the cheap way to make a hundred identical quads stop looking identical.
kill = the particle ends on contact (a raindrop); settle = it stops where it landed, holds, then fades (snow).

hold.description: settle only: seconds a landed particle rests before fading.

fade.description: settle only: seconds the fade-out takes.

offset.description: Height above the ground a landed particle rests at.

splash.description: Emitters to burst at the contact point — a raindrop's splash. A comma-separated list of entity ids or tags, each optionally `*n` for n particles (`weather-splash-ring,weather-splash*3` = one ring plus three droplets per drop). Those emitters usually have rate 0 and are fired only by this.

splashChance.description: Fraction of landings that splash. Heavy rain lands more than a thousand drops a second and a splash for every one of them is both a fill-rate bill and visually WRONG — real rain reads as scattered rings, not a continuous sheet. 0.1–0.2 for a downpour.

palette.description: Override the element's palette. Omitted = the element's own.

feel.description: Aesthetic bias used when this spell was generated.

effect.description: What the payload DOES, as a look: root (vines, chains, holds), stun (stars, chains overhead), slow (hourglass, drips), haste (chevrons, speed lines), shield (hex wards), heal (crosses, rising motes), shadow (dark matter, fading).

channelled.description: buff/debuff: the aura holds for the duration while the caster channels, then fades. Off = the effect flashes when it lands and lingers only briefly.

shape.description: The volume. point = no volume (a single target, the caster).

radius.description: Metres. circle: radius; cone: reach; line: length; point: a body size. The REFERENCE size every visual scales from.

range.description: Metres from the caster the volume is centred at. 0 = on the caster.

windup.description: Seconds from cast start to the payload resolving.

duration.description: Sustained kinds (beam, zone, channel, pulse, buff, summon, portal): seconds the effect holds.

ticksPerSecond.description: Sustained kinds: payload applications per second.

growTo.description: Lingering volumes that grow: the final radius.

height.description: Vertical extent of the volume, metres either side.

intensity.description: How big a deal this spell is — drives module count, light, shake, and how much budget it may spend.

sheet.description: Spritesheet data-asset id. Its grid is the flipbook: columns are frames, rows are colour variants.

row.description: Sheet row. 5 is the greyscale variant in the purchased library — leave it and let `color` tint.

size.description: Metres — the quad's width; height follows `aspect`.
