orient.description: billboard faces the camera; ground lies flat (marks, runes); vertical stands upright and yaws toward the camera (a slash, a wave); facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); velocity aligns with the anchor's motion.

spin.description: Radians/sec the quad turns in its own plane. Lying on the ground that is a yaw; standing up it is a roll around a horizontal axis, which reads wrong on most symbols — the symbol catalog says which may.

yaw.description: Fixed rotation around the facing axis, radians.

randomYaw.description: Roll `yaw` per play — cheap variety for repeated impacts.

cell.description: [col, row] of ONE sheet cell shown as a static SYMBOL (a sigil, a glyph, an arrow) instead of playing the sheet as a flipbook. `fps`/`loop` are ignored; the symbol lives for `duration` (0 = the phase, or 0.6 s).

orbit.description: Metres the quad circles the anchor at, around its up axis. 0 = sits on the anchor.

orbitSpeed.description: Radians/sec along the orbit; negative runs the other way.

orbitPhase.description: Starting angle on the orbit, radians (0 = in front of the anchor). `repeat.turn` advances it per copy.

emitter.description: The emitter, in the `particles` component's own vocabulary. colorStart/colorEnd are overridden by the module's `color`/`colorEnd` unless they are left white.

burst.description: Particles spawned the moment the module starts.

stream.description: Keep emitting at the emitter's `rate` for the module's duration — channels, trails, auras.

radius.description: Outer radius in metres at scale 1.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer. 0 = a filled disc (a rune, a portal floor).

orient.description: ground lies on the terrain; vertical stands upright yawed toward the camera; facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); billboard faces the camera.

expand.description: Scale at birth and at death: a shockwave runs 0.1 → 1, a rune holds 1 → 1. `sizeCurve` overrides.

soft.description: Edge softness. 0 is a hard band; 1 fades across the whole width.

texture.description: Texture asset id laid across the disc (a rune, a sigil). Omitted = a procedural soft band.

arc.description: Degrees of the disc that are drawn, centred on the spell direction: 360 is a full ring, 90 a wedge in front of the caster.

noise.description: Breaks the band with scrolling noise so it reads as energy rather than a drawn circle.

swirl.description: Spiral distortion strength — the portal look. 0 = none.

drape.description: Ground rings follow the terrain under them (needs the host's ground probe).

height.description: Vertical/billboard: metres above the anchor the centre sits.

style.description: energy = noisy fresnel rim (barriers, orbs, charge-ups); glass = clean thin rim (bubbles, wards); smoke = dense normal-blended body (a cloud, a void); wire = a lattice of noise lines (arcane cages).

fresnel.description: Rim power — higher is a thinner, brighter edge. 0 = flat.

noise.description: How much scrolling 3D noise breaks the surface.

dissolve.description: [[t, threshold]] — the surface burns away where noise < threshold. A curve 0 → 1 is a shell that dissolves as it dies; 1 → 0 is one that assembles.

squash.description: Vertical scale: a dome on the ground is ~0.6, a tall bubble 1.4.

radius.description: Base radius, metres.

topRadius.description: Radius at the far end. Omitted = same as `radius` (a pillar); 0 = a cone to a point.

orient.description: up = a pillar out of the ground; forward = a cone along the spell direction (breath, spray); down = hanging from the sky onto the anchor.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed along the axis; positive = base → far end.

edgeFade.description: Fade at the silhouette so the tube has no hard vertical edges.

capFade.description: Fraction of the height faded out at the base and at the far end.

length.description: Metres along the spell direction when there is no target (or `toTarget` is off).

toTarget.description: Span anchor → target when the frame has one.

core.description: Bright inner core as a fraction of width. 0 = none.

style.description: energy = soft noisy glow; laser = hard clean edge; plasma = fat writhing body.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed toward the far end, metres/sec.

jitter.description: Metres of sideways displacement per segment.

refreshHz.description: How often the path re-rolls — the flicker.

count.description: Independent strands, each with its own path — a channelled storm rather than one arc.

spread.description: count > 1: metres the far ends scatter around the target.

arc.description: line = anchor to target/direction; sky = strikes DOWN onto the anchor from `length` metres up; ground = crawls along the terrain outward from the anchor in a random direction.

intensityCurve.description: [[t, multiplier]]. Default is a flash: spike, then decay.

asset.description: Model asset id. Omitted = the procedural `primitive`.

primitive.description: Procedural bodies for when no model is given.

motion.description: drop = falls from `from` metres up and lands as the module ends; rise = comes up out of the ground; hover = bobs in place; orbit = circles the anchor; launch = flies up and away; forward = glides `from` metres along the spell direction (a projection, an afterimage).

from.description: drop: start height above the anchor; rise: depth below it. 0 = auto.

spread.description: count > 1: radius they scatter or orbit within.

tint.description: Colour the body with the palette; off keeps the asset's own material.

length.description: Seconds of history the ribbon covers.

radius.description: circle: radius; cone: reach; line: length. Metres.

windup.description: Seconds the fill takes to reach the rim — the clock the target reads.

hold.description: Seconds the volume stays live after the windup.

growFrom.description: Live volumes that GROW: scale at the start of the hold, reaching 1 at its end.

curtain.description: Height of the vertical curtain, metres. 0 = auto from radius.

rimOpacity.description: The rim is the only number a dodge is judged against — keep it the brightest part, but not blown out.

dash.description: Rim dashing, 0..1: 0 is a solid band, 0.5 draws dashes as long as their gaps — the PSX marker look.

height.description: Vertical extent the drape is clamped to — keep it equal to the hit test's `delivery.height`.

radius.description: Outer reach of the arc, metres.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer: near 1 a thin crescent, near 0 a fat cleave.

sweep.description: Degrees the arc covers, centred on the spell direction.

tilt.description: Roll of the cutting plane around the spell direction: 0 = a horizontal cleave, 90 = a vertical overhead chop, ±45 diagonal.

reverse.description: Sweep the other way (right-to-left for a cleave, bottom-to-top for a chop).

sweepTime.description: Fraction of the life the leading edge takes to cross the arc; the rest is the tail fading out.

tail.description: Length of the trailing fade behind the leading edge, as a fraction of the sweep.

height.description: Metres above the anchor the arc's centre sits (chest height for a cleave).

core.description: How bright the leading edge is, toward the glow colour.

strength.description: Metres of camera displacement felt by a camera at the effect.

range.description: Metres over which the shake fades out. A camera at the effect feels the full `strength`, one at `range` or further feels nothing (quadratic falloff between). 0 disables the falloff — every camera in the world shakes, which is almost never what you want.

__schema19.description: Stable key so a human tweak or an agent's note can name this module.

__schema21.description: The library preset this came from — provenance for tweak-and-regenerate, never read at runtime.

at.description: origin = where the spell resolves (the volume's centre, the impact point); caster = the casting body; target = the targeted body or point; path = the projectile in flight (travel phase); ground = origin projected onto the terrain.

socket.description: caster/target only: a named attach point — rightHand, leftHand, chest, head, feet — resolved by the host to a bone-socket entity under that body. A missing socket falls back to the body itself.

offset.description: metres in the anchor's own frame: x right, y up, z FORWARD along the spell direction.

follow.description: Keep tracking the anchor for the module's whole life (a hand mid-swing, a projectile in flight) instead of sampling it once at start.

__schema30.description: Seconds it lives. 0 = natural length (a flipbook's frames, a burst's longest particle) or, for sustained kinds, the phase length.

__schema34.description: Where colour fades toward over life, for kinds that fade (particles, trail, beam core).

__schema36.description: additive = light (nearly everything magical); normal = matter that occludes (smoke, a poison cloud).

__schema43.description: PSX look: quantise the procedural shading to this many cells across the shape (0 = off, 16–32 reads as pixel art). Rings, shells, columns and beams snap their noise and bands to the grid; masks and sprites switch to nearest filtering.

__schema45.description: Alpha steps (0 = smooth). 3–5 turns soft falloffs into hard bands — the other half of the PSX look.

__schema47.description: [[t, multiplier]] over life, on top of the module's own size.

__schema50.description: Play this module as a STEPPING sequence — spikes that erupt one after another along the strike, a column of circles, glyphs spread around the caster. The sequencer expands it into `count` copies; the audit counts them.

count.description: Copies played. 1 = the module plays once.

every.description: Seconds between copies — the STEP. Nothing tweens between them; each copy appears whole.

step.description: Metres each copy moves on from the last, in the spell frame (x right, y up, z forward): [0,0,1.4] marches spikes away from the caster, [0,0.5,0] stacks rings into a column.

turn.description: Degrees each copy is turned around the anchor's up axis relative to the last. With `step` [0,0,r] and turn 360/count the copies stand in a circle; on an orbiting sprite it advances the orbit phase instead.

alternate.description: Flip the spin (and a slash's tilt) on every other copy — a column of circles turning against each other.

scale.description: Size multiplier applied per copy: 0.85 tapers a stack, 1.3 steps a shockwave outward.

jitter.description: Metres of seeded horizontal scatter added to each copy.

spread.description: Half-angle, in degrees, that each particle's launch direction is randomised within — on ANY shape, unlike coneAngle. 0 fires every particle along `direction` in exact parallel, which is right for a jet and wrong for anything suspended: a box of specks all falling parallel reads as SNOW. 180 is a full sphere, the usual choice for dust hanging in the air.

turbulence.description: Strength of a smooth per-particle wander field, units/sec^2. This is what makes dust look airborne rather than falling — motes curl past each other instead of tracking straight lines. Pair it with `drag` so the wander stays a drift instead of accumulating into a drift-off.

turbulenceSpeed.description: How fast the wander field evolves. Low (~0.2) is a lazy indoor drift; high is agitated.

fadeIn.description: Fraction of each particle's life spent ramping up from nothing to `opacityStart`. Anything meant to already be there — dust, fog, embers — needs this: with 0 every particle POPS into existence at full strength, which is the single clearest tell that an ambient effect is being spawned at you.

radial.description: Aim each particle along the line from the emitter's centre to its own spawn point instead of along `direction`: out = an explosion (needs a sphere/box shape so there IS an offset); in = energy CONVERGING on the centre — the charge-up look, particles born on the shell and flying inward. `spread` still scatters around that line.

sprite.description: The procedural sprite used when no `texture` is given: soft = a radial falloff (smoke, glow); square = a hard-edged square with a one-texel fade (PSX sparks and rain); pixel = a chunky 6x6 blob with stepped alpha (retro embers, motes); flame = an 8x8 pixel-art flame tongue pointing up the screen (PSX fire); ring = a hollow annulus, which is what a splash on the ground actually looks like (pair it with `orient: ground` and a growing `sizeCurve`); streak = a vertical tapered line for rain and sparks (pair it with `orient: velocity`); noise = a torn, cloudy puff with real internal structure, for anything big and slow that would otherwise read as a smooth grey blob — dust banks, smoke fronts (give a noise puff some `spin`: the structure is only visible because it turns). Every sprite but soft is nearest-filtered, so its texels stay hard at any size.

filter.description: Magnification of a `texture` sheet. nearest keeps low-res pixel-art sheets hard-edged (the PSX look); linear smears them. The procedural sprites choose their own filtering and ignore this.

steps.description: PSX banding: colour, size and opacity change in this many hard jumps over a particle's life instead of gliding (each step shows the value at its middle). 0 = smooth. 3–5 is the retro look — a flame that goes white, orange, red, gone reads as 1998; one that fades through every shade in between does not.

snap.description: PSX grid snap, in metres: rendered positions snap to a world grid of this size and quad sizes to multiples of it (a living particle never snaps below one cell). The same wobble as PSX vertex precision. 0 = off. Size it to the effect — around a fifth of the particle size — or it reads as a lattice.

frameRate.description: PSX stepping: the simulation advances in whole ticks of 1/frameRate seconds, so particles jump rather than slide (billboards still face the camera every frame). 0 = every frame. 8–15 is the retro range; flames at 12, lazy smoke lower.

subUV.description: Play the texture as a SPRITE SHEET, per particle. A still sprite drifting is the clearest tell that an effect is dated — every modern smoke, fire or impact particle animates on its own clock.

softFade.description: Metres over which a particle fades as it approaches solid geometry. 0 = off. A quad slicing visibly into the ground is THE thing that reads as cheap, and nothing else fixes it. Costs a scene-depth read, so leave it off for effects that never touch a surface (sparks in mid-air) — and NEVER pair it with `orient: ground`, which lies a quad centimetres above the surface behind it: the fade then measures that gap and erases the whole thing, which looks exactly like the effect failing to spawn.

stretch.description: Stretch each particle along its own velocity, in seconds of travel. 0 = round. Sparks and debris read as DOTS without this — the streak is the motion.

orient.description: What each quad points at. camera = the usual billboard, always square to the viewer. velocity = the quad's long axis is locked to the particle's WORLD velocity and it spins about that axis to face the camera — the difference between rain that falls the way the wind blows and rain that tilts with wherever you happen to be looking, which is what camera+`stretch` gives you (that one rolls the billboard by the SCREEN-space velocity, so the streaks swing as you turn and never foreshorten). ground = laid flat in the XZ plane, facing up: splash rings, ripples, scorch marks. upright = billboard that turns about Y only, so a tall quad stays vertical when you look up — dust banks, distant haze.

sizeCurve.description: [[t, size], …] over normalized life, overriding sizeStart/sizeEnd. A two-point lerp cannot describe a flash — spike, fast falloff, long dim tail — which is most of what separates an impact from a fading blob.

opacityCurve.description: [[t, opacity], …] over normalized life, overriding opacityStart/End and fadeIn.

space.description: world = particles trail behind a moving emitter; local = they ride it.

ground.description: Terrain contact. The host answers 'how high is the ground here' from the streamed terrain, sampled once per particle at birth; a particle that falls to it dies or settles. Terrain only — props, roofs and water are not tested. Needs space: world. Settled particles count toward `max`, so a settling snowfall wants a large one.

mode.description: life = play the sheet once across the particle's lifetime (smoke that billows and dissipates); loop = play it repeatedly at `fps`; random = hold one frame chosen per particle, which is the cheap way to make a hundred identical quads stop looking identical.
kill = the particle ends on contact (a raindrop); settle = it stops where it landed, holds, then fades (snow).

hold.description: settle only: seconds a landed particle rests before fading.

fade.description: settle only: seconds the fade-out takes.

offset.description: Height above the ground a landed particle rests at.

splash.description: Emitters to burst at the contact point — a raindrop's splash. A comma-separated list of entity ids or tags, each optionally `*n` for n particles (`weather-splash-ring,weather-splash*3` = one ring plus three droplets per drop). Those emitters usually have rate 0 and are fired only by this.

splashChance.description: Fraction of landings that splash. Heavy rain lands more than a thousand drops a second and a splash for every one of them is both a fill-rate bill and visually WRONG — real rain reads as scattered rings, not a continuous sheet. 0.1–0.2 for a downpour.

item.description: An item definition (assets/items/<id>.json). Inventories hold { itemId, qty } stacks — one cell each — that point here, so editing a file updates every copy.

__schema2.description: Broad category for filtering and UI grouping; `slots` decides wearability, not this.

__schema4.description: Slot kinds this item may be worn in (a one-handed sword: [primary, secondary]; a charm: [trinket] fits either trinket slot). Empty = carry-only.

__schema6.description: Maximum quantity per stack (one grid cell). 1 = unique instances (every piece of gear).

__schema8.description: Kilograms per unit; carried AND worn items count against capacity.

__schema11.description: Texture asset id (assets/textures/…) drawn in the inventory cell; absent = the name's initials.

__schema13.description: Accent colour for the cell/tooltip; defaults to the rarity colour.

__schema15.description: Flat additions applied while WORN: attributes (strength…) feed the formulas, derived stats (maxHp, armor…) add after them.

__schema17.description: Minimums to equip, checked against the character's level and EFFECTIVE attributes (base + allocated + worn).

__schema19.description: For `bag`-slot items: the grid this bag grants while worn. A bag must be empty to be swapped or removed.

__schema21.description: Held in BOTH hands (a greatsword, a greataxe, a staff, a bow). While it is worn in `primary`, the `offhand` item stays equipped but INACTIVE: no modifiers, not drawn, no stance (it still counts toward weight). The offhand slot shows greyed out. Nothing is unequipped either way.

__schema23.description: Animation STANCES this item puts its wielder in while held, most specific first — a greataxe: ["Axe2H", "TwoHanded"] borrows every two-handed clip it has no axe version of. The character then plays `<Stance>_<clip>` wherever its model has one (GreatSword_Run, Staff_Attack1, SwordShield_Death). An off-hand item's stance COMBINES with the main hand's: a Sword with a Shield is "SwordShield", then "Sword". Read by the `weapon-stance` script. Empty = no stance (a ring, a potion).

__schema26.description: How this item LOOKS when worn: a choice of parts from a modular model plus a theme sheet. Presentation only — drawn by the `equipment-look` builtin on whatever entity holds the model (a sword in a hand socket), and absent for items with no visible form. Two items can share parts and differ by sheet, or share a sheet and differ by parts.

model.description: Model asset id of the UBERMESH this look is cut from (assets/models/…). The entity that shows it must already draw this model — a look changes parts and texture, never the model.

parts.description: Part NAMES to show, as the model's own part table spells them (unwrap-weapon writes it into the glTF and beside it as <model>-parts.json): one of each family for a weapon — a blade, a guard, a collar, a pommel, the grip. Every other part is hidden. Empty = nothing shows.

texture.description: Texture asset id of the theme sheet (assets/textures/…) — an atlas registered against this model's key. Absent = the sheet baked into the model.

glow.description: Emissive glow on an item. Costs no draw call on a batched (`moving`) model: it is a per-instance value in the same batch as every other item of that model.

effects.description: Standing effects this item carries while it is shown: embers off a blade, frost mist round a guard, a light at a staff's head. Each is a `vfx` asset played for as long as the item is equipped, at a point ON the item that follows it through every swing.

__schema30.description: Emissive colour added on top of the item's own texture.

__schema31.description: Multiplier on `color`. Above ~1 it reads as light; with bloom on it blooms.

__schema33.description: Part NAMES that glow (a blade, not its grip). Omitted = every part the item shows.

__schema35.description: Breathe the glow instead of holding it steady.

min.description: Fraction of full glow at the bottom of a pulse.

__schema39.description: Make the glow MOVE: pixelated noise scrolling over the glowing parts, stepped at 12 fps in 4 bands — the PSX look of the fire overlays. Omitted = a steady glow.

amount.description: 0 = a flat, even glow; 1 = all moving noise (dark gaps between the hot licks). The overlay the fire's ember bed uses.

scale.description: Noise cells across the WHOLE texture sheet — a blade is a thin strip of it, so this wants to be about the sheet's texel count (128 on a 128 px sheet = one cell per texel). Much lower and a blade gets one or two cells.

flow.description: Sheet-heights per second the noise runs along the part. Positive runs toward the blade's TIP (fire climbing), negative toward the guard (poison creeping down); 0 churns in place.

threshold.description: Noise below this adds nothing. High (0.7+) = sparse glints; low = a wash.

churn.description: How fast the pattern EVOLVES in place, on top of `flow`. 1 = the fire overlay's boil; 0.2–0.4 = a slow, oily creep (poison); 0 = a frozen pattern that only scrolls.

frameRate.description: Steps per second the noise advances in (PSX chop). Lower = choppier and slower-looking; 12 matches the fire.

__schema47.description: Fade the glow along the item's length (model +Y — a blade's base to its point): { from: 0.55, to: 0.85 } puts poison on only the last third of the blade, feathered in. With `noise` the edge dissolves through the moving heat rather than a straight line. Batched (`moving`) models only.

from.description: Where along the glowing parts' LENGTH (0 = base, 1 = tip) the glow starts from nothing.

to.description: Where it reaches full strength. Set it below `from` to fade toward the tip instead.

__schema52.description: A standing effect an item carries.

__schema53.description: vfx data-asset id (assets/vfx/<id>.json) — WHAT plays: which particles, their sprite or texture, size, opacity, colour ramp, rate, lifetime, plus rings, shells, beams or a light. The same assets as torches and spells. Keep item effects in one folder (e.g. `items/embers`) so every item using one is ONE asset: particles are batched by look, so a hundred ember swords draw their embers in one call.

__schema54.description: Material asset whose colours are the effect's palette (color → primary, emissive → glow, color darkened → secondary) — recolour an effect without copying it. Omitted = the effect's own element palette.

__schema56.description: A point on an item's model.

__schema57.description: Part NAME of the model (its part table). Omitted = the box of every part the item shows.

__schema59.description: Point in the part's bounding box. "tip"/"base" are the two ends of its LONGEST axis (a blade's point and its root; the ends of a guard's bar), "center" its middle. Or [x, y, z] fractions of the box in the model's own axes, 0..1 on each — [0.5, 0.9, 0.5] is nine tenths of the way up a blade. This is how an emitter is pinpointed.

__schema61.description: Nudge after `at`, in METRES along the model's own axes (they turn with the item).

__schema63.description: item = the effect turns with the item: its modules' offsets, emitter volume and `direction` are in the MODEL's axes — on the longsword +Y runs up the blade toward the tip, ±Z out of the two edges, ±X off the flats — so "up the blade" stays up the blade through every swing. world = upright in the world (yaw only), like a torch. Gravity is always world-down either way, so drips fall and flames rise.

__schema65.description: Size every particle emitter's volume (box/sphere half-extents) to the anchor part's box, so particles are born along the WHOLE blade instead of at one point. [x, y, z] scales each axis — [1, 0.5, 1] is half the blade's length (pair it with anchor at [0.5, 0.75, 0.5] for the upper half); 0 on an axis flattens it. false = the effect's own shapeSize.

__schema67.description: Metres from the camera past which the effect stops simulating (fades out, and back in on approach).

progression.description: Levelling and stat rules (assets/progression/<id>.json). One per game; a character-sheet script names it by id.

__schema0.description: Level cap. Experience past the cap is kept but grants nothing.

__schema2.description: Attribute points granted per level gained; the player spends them one at a time.

__schema4.description: Where every attribute starts at level 1, before any points are spent.

__schema6.description: Experience to go from level L to L+1 = round(base × growth^(L−1)).

__schema8.description: The grid every character always has, bag or no bag.

__schema10.description: Authority-enforced inventory action times. One action per character; destinations and ownership are rechecked at completion.

transfer.description: Seconds for moving or splitting stacks between bag and pockets; rearranging within a container is immediate.

equip.description: Seconds before an equipment change takes effect, including replacing worn gear.

unequip.description: Seconds before removing worn gear takes effect.

__schema16.description: base + Σ coefficient × effective attribute; worn-item modifiers add after.

game-hud.description: Game HUD skin, equipment layout, audio and navigation policy. Quest areas are compass-only; maps never contain quests or other POIs.

__schema2.description: CSS nine-slice: slice is measured in SOURCE pixels; border is the displayed width. Preserve alpha outside ornaments and keep corner proportions fixed.

__schema6.description: Edge sampling only; corner ornaments always retain their proportions. Use repeat with a seamless straight rail crop.

__schema13.description: Local chat receive filters and detached-window preferences. Filters operate only on messages delivered to this player; they never change server routing or membership.

__schema20.description: Status artwork at source dimensions. Bar rectangles [x,y,width,height] clip the fill without scaling its texture as values change.

clockEntity.description: Entity owning the day-night script; HUD reads its live dayNightHour so offline and replicated clocks match the sky.

compassResponseMs.description: Visual heading smoothing time constant, in milliseconds; zero follows the camera immediately. Rendered every animation frame with wrap-safe angles.

quest.description: Quest definition. Progress belongs to authority-owned quest journals, not this asset.

__schema5.description: Approximate search region [world X, world Z], never an exact objective marker. Only the compass may visualize this region.

tooltip.description: Presentation-only tooltip. Text is rendered literally, never as HTML.

theme.description: A theme data asset: the complete per-location skin. One dungeon plan + N themes = N locations. Generate the engine material docs from it with materialsForTheme(); resolve mesh world-UV scales with uvScaleFor().

__schema0.description: Human-readable theme name, e.g. "The Ossuary Vaults".

__schema1.description: One or two sentences of art direction — what this location should feel like.

__schema3.description: The colours this theme's light fixtures CAST — part of the dressing vocabulary, not the layout. Dressing passes read these when placing lights so a re-skin changes the light along with the walls.

__schema4.description: Colour cast by this theme's warm fixtures (torches, braziers, hearths).

__schema6.description: Colour cast by this theme's cold sources (moonlight shafts, fungus, sorcery).

__schema7.description: Colour cast by accent-slot fixtures (runes, crystals, shrines) — pairs with the `accent` slot.

__schema8.description: Role slot → texture set. Compilers and dressing passes reference SLOTS, never material ids, so swapping the theme re-skins everything built from the same plan.

__schema9.description: Walkable worked surfaces — room floors, corridor floors.

__schema10.description: Texture asset id — the relative path under assets/textures/ INCLUDING extension (e.g. "crypt-a/mossy-brick-wall.png"), which is how the asset loader keys textures. Omit for a flat-colour slot (graybox, or a slot this location genuinely leaves untextured).

__schema12.description: Base colour, multiplied with `map` when one is set (leave #ffffff to show the texture untinted; darken it to grime a whole slot). With no `map` this IS the slot's look.

__schema13.description: PBR roughness 0..1. Omitted = engine material default (0.85, near-matte — right for stone). Set it low only on slots that should read wet or polished.

__schema15.description: PBR metalness 0..1. Omitted = engine material default (0.05). Really only the `metal` slot wants a high value; metallic stone reads as oily.

__schema17.description: Texture asset id of a tangent-space normal map (OpenGL +Y convention), same id form as `map`. Shares `map`'s UV transform, so the theme's single `uvScale` covers both.

__schema19.description: METRES PER TEXTURE TILE [u, v] in world space — NOT a UV repeat count. [3, 3] = one tile every 3 m. REQUIRED whenever `map` is set: the shell materials generated from a theme pin `repeat` to [1, 1] and the mesh carries `uv: { mode: "world", scale }` instead, so this value is what keeps a re-skin from silently changing the texture's world size (the counting-stones bug). Compilers read it with `uvScaleFor(theme, slot)` and bake it into the mesh they emit.

__schema22.description: One role slot: which texture set a semantic surface role wears in this theme, plus the metres-per-tile that keeps its world scale stable across re-skins.

__schema24.description: Overhead shell surfaces — flat ceilings and vault faces.

__schema25.description: Carved edging: door frames, cornices, balustrades, pilasters — the detail band between shell slots.

__schema26.description: The theme's signature flourish — runes, bone, glow, gilt. Small doses; pairs with light.accent.

__schema27.description: Natural/unworked stone — cave walls, tunnel shells, rubble, stalagmites. The other half of the worked/natural mix; transition assemblies blend wall→rock.

__schema28.description: Structural and prop timber — beams, planking, crates, scaffolds.

__schema29.description: Ironmongery — grates, hinges, sconces, portcullises, banding.

__schema30.description: Stair treads and risers. Separate from `floor` because steps are cut pieces that read best with their own tighter texture, and stairs are exactly where a wrong uvScale is most visible.

__schema31.description: Water surfaces, when this location has any. The only optional slot — many dungeons are dry.

peerId.description: Its owner's peer id (the character id on a cluster).

name.description: Region name, what the player reads.

from.description: Region id left, or null when the body was in no zone.

hitreg.armor-atlas.name: Armor / Weapon Atlas
hitreg.armor-atlas.description: Register generated artwork against a UV key and write a game-ready atlas. Character armor uses a 256px sheet; longsword weapons use a 128px sheet with weapon-sized bleed by default.

key.label: UV key
key.description: The flat PNG color-key sheet supplied to the image generator.

art.label: Generated art
art.description: The generated PNG painted over the key layout. It must have exactly the same dimensions as the UV key.

sheet.label: Sheet
sheet.description: Which key this art was painted over. Character armor defaults to 256px output; longsword defaults to 128px output. Each sheet has its own slot table.

name.label: Output name
name.description: Texture id below assets/textures; folders are allowed. The .png suffix is added automatically.

size.label: Atlas size
size.description: Square output size in pixels. Presets are character armor 256px and longsword 128px; set this only when intentionally overriding the sheet preset.

bleed.label: Bleed
bleed.description: Padding texels dilated around UV islands. Presets are armor 8px and longsword 3px, keeping the same relative gutter after downsampling.

filter.label: Filter
filter.description: Box filtering is the normal downsampling path; nearest preserves hard source pixels.

slices.label: Keep slices
slices.description: Write per-island diagnostic PNGs into the local tool-run record.

artMargin.label: Artwork margin
artMargin.description: Include artwork outside the keyed islands when estimating registration.

skip.label: Skip regions
skip.description: Optional comma-separated island names that are absent from this set, such as hood,ornament.

hitreg.wfc-3d.name: 3D Prefab WFC
hitreg.wfc-3d.description: Collapse a 3D tile grid into a reusable composite prefab. Every occupied cell is a nested prefab instance; the tool never emits raw geometry. Tilesets are hand-authored (exact socket matching) or LEARNED from a modelled kit by tools/wfc-3d/kit.mjs (parts + example structures in, atlased modules + cell prefabs + a tileset with learned face pairs out).

tileset.label: Prefab tileset
tileset.description: JSON describing prefab tiles, their six face sockets, weights, allowed Y rotations, optional boundary sockets, and pinned cells — or a learned tileset written by the kit importer (assets/wfc/<kit>.tileset.json), which adds allowed face pairs, an outside tile and UV-alignment overrides. See tools/wfc-3d/README.md.

name.label: Output prefab
name.description: Prefab id below assets/prefabs; folders are allowed. The .json suffix is added automatically.

height.label: Height (Y)
height.description: Grid cells along world Y. Use 1 for a single-layer layout.

attempts.label: Retry attempts
attempts.description: Fresh deterministic collapses attempted after contradictions.

origin.label: Prefab origin
origin.description: Centered keeps the composite anchor at the bottom-center; minimum starts cell 0 at the anchor.

hitreg.mesh-dc.name: Blender to DC
hitreg.mesh-dc.description: Import grouped Blender solids as editable volumes with their original palette and an entrance anchor.

source.label: Blender mesh export
source.description: JSON created by the Blender exporter. Each group becomes an editable volume.

name.label: Output name
name.description: A new name for the imported assets.

voxelSize.label: Surface resolution (m)
voxelSize.description: Smaller values preserve finer details and take longer to load.

maxCells.label: Maximum cells per group
maxCells.description: Limits import size. Split oversized groups or increase surface resolution.

materialId.label: Palette material ID
materialId.description: Optional new material ID. Defaults to the output name followed by /dc-palette.

group.label: Group name
group.description: Optional exact group name. Leave empty to import all groups.

default.description: Value used when an instance does not set this prop.

bindings.description: Where the value is written on expand: "<localEntityId>/components/<component>/<field>".

description.description: What this knob does, in one line — shown as inspector help and read by agents.

kind.description: Control type. Omit to infer from `default` (and from `options`, which implies enum).

label.description: Human-facing name. Omit to use the prop key.

group.description: Inspector section, e.g. "Handling" or "Damage". Ungrouped knobs come first.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound — with max, renders a slider.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound — with min, renders a slider.

unit.description: Unit suffix shown beside the value: "m", "m/s", "deg", "rpm", "%".

options.description: Allowed values — presence implies an enum dropdown.

assetKind.description: For kind "asset": which library to pick from ("material", "model", "prefab", …).

advanced.description: Hide behind the inspector's “advanced” disclosure; agents still see it.

name.description: Project id. Must match the folder name under projects/, since asset ids namespace by it.

title.description: Display name in the editor's project picker (e.g. "MMO"); the folder name when unset.

group.description: Editor project-picker group, e.g. "MMO", "Dungeons", "DC reference". Projects sharing a group list together; ungrouped projects list last.

menuOrder.description: Sort key in the project picker, lower first. A group sorts by its lowest member; unset sorts after set, then by name.

scenes.description: The editor's scene menu for this project, in order; the first entry is the main scene. Scene files on disk that no entry names still appear, under "other", so a new scene is never hidden.

id.description: Scene file id: the path under assets/scenes/ without .scene.json (e.g. "arena", "hollow-bastion/deepwake"). The file is the scene's identity; the doc's own `name` field is not.

label.description: What the menu shows instead of the id, e.g. "Combat lab" for arena.

note.description: One line on what the scene is for; shown as the menu tooltip.

variants.description: Pipeline stages or alternates of this scene (blockout, undercoat, editable, …). They list under it instead of as separate scenes; the menu labels each by what its id adds to the base id.

items.description: Scene file id: the path under assets/scenes/ without .scene.json (e.g. "arena", "hollow-bastion/deepwake"). The file is the scene's identity; the doc's own `name` field is not.

engine.description: Engine version or range this project was built against. Advisory.

multiplayer.description: How this game is played together. "p2p": the engine's peer rooms (a tab hosts; fine for co-op, prototypes, anything where a host cheating costs nobody). "server": dedicated/layered servers ONLY — the playground never forms a peer room for this project's scenes (a tab with no server plays alone), because a peer host is authoritative over everything it simulates. An MMO with a persistent world declares "server".

devConsole.description: Whether a PUBLISHED build of this game contains the developer console (/time, /weather, whatever its scripts declare). "dev": the editor has it, published bundles do not — the console module is not compiled in at all, so there is nothing for a player to find. "always": ship it (an internal build, a playtest bundle you want to drive from the chat box). "never": not even in the editor, for a game whose own scripts must not be pokeable. tools/publish.mjs reads this; --console / --no-console override it for one build.

tools.description: Registered tools this project needs installed under the engine's tools/ folder.

repo.description: Where to get it — a git URL or other clone/install source. Shown when it is missing.

version.description: Version or range the project was built against. Advisory: nothing enforces it yet.

optional.description: True if the project still runs without it (the tool only regenerates content).

reason.description: What this project uses it for. Worth writing: it is what tells a reader whether they need it.
